scenarios.title: Capture screenshot on passing test when using screenshot configuration
given: A test suite contains passing tests
A dedicated Playwright configuration file configured to force screenshots for every test while preserving default project settings is available
scenarios.when: Tests are executed from the command line specifying the dedicated configuration file via the --config flag
then: A screenshot artifact is generated and saved for each passing test

scenarios.title: Capture screenshot on failing test when using screenshot configuration
given: A test suite contains a failing test
A dedicated Playwright configuration file configured to force screenshots for every test while preserving default project settings is available
scenarios.when: Tests are executed from the command line specifying the dedicated configuration file via the --config flag
then: The test failure is reported in the test execution output
A screenshot artifact is generated and saved for the failing test

scenarios.title: Preserve project and browser settings from default configuration
given: The default Playwright configuration defines multiple projects and environment settings
The dedicated screenshot configuration file inherits default project configurations
scenarios.when: Tests are executed using the dedicated screenshot configuration file via the --config flag
then: Tests are executed across each project configured in the default configuration
Configured project-level base URLs, timeouts, and device parameters match the default configuration settings

scenarios.title: Default configuration execution retains original screenshot behavior on passing tests
given: A test suite contains passing tests
The default Playwright configuration is used
scenarios.when: Tests are executed without specifying the custom screenshot configuration
then: No screenshot artifacts are created for the passing tests

scenarios.title: Execution with non-existent configuration file fails with an error
given: The command-line test runner is available
scenarios.when: Tests are executed from the command line with the --config flag pointing to a non-existent configuration file (e.g. missing.config.ts)
then: The test execution exits with an error status
An error message indicating that the specified configuration file cannot be found is displayed
